title: Lines
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Lines are practical: a ruler, a set square and a pair of compasses in the child's hands. The tutor talks the child through the drawing and asks them to check it (measure the gap at both ends, measure the right angle, measure both halves). Lines in the classroom (window frames, ruled lines, the corner of a door) come first.

skills.key_step: The child says parallel lines stay the same distance apart all along, and checks by measuring the gap at two places.

floor.prerequisite: Picks out parallel lines in pictures.
floor.question: Are the ruled lines in an exercise book parallel?

representations: railway lines, ruled lines, a window frame
two lines with the gap measured at both ends
a set square sliding along a ruler
steps: Look for two lines that never meet.
Measure the gap at one end and the other.
If the gaps are equal, the lines are parallel; length does not matter.
To draw them, slide a set square along a ruler without turning it.

board.do: Draw two lines, 2 cm apart at the left and 4 cm apart at the right.

board.say: Is the gap the same at both ends?

board.do: Wait for the child to say no.
Ask whether the lines would meet if they were longer.
Ask the child to draw two parallel lines with a ruler and a set square.

misconceptions.ask: Is the gap the same at both ends?
misconceptions.repair: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart.

misconceptions.ask: Are the edges of a slanting ladder parallel?
misconceptions.repair: Parallel lines can point any way.

misconceptions.ask: Does length change the gap between them?
misconceptions.repair: Length does not matter, only the gap.

misconceptions.ask: Did the set square turn as it moved?
misconceptions.repair: Slide the set square along the ruler without turning it.

checks.question: Are the two rails of a railway line parallel?
Two lines are 2 cm apart at one end and 4 cm apart at the other. Are they parallel?

skills.key_step: The child says that bisecting cuts a line into two equal halves and that the perpendicular bisector meets it at its midpoint at a right angle, drawn with arcs of the same radius, more than half the line, from both ends.
representations: a strip of paper folded end to end
a line with arcs from both ends crossing above and below
steps: Open the compasses to more than half the line.
Draw arcs above and below from one end.
Keep the same opening and draw arcs from the other end.
Join the crossings; check equal halves and a right angle.
contexts: marking the centre line of a pitch
folding a paper in a craft lesson

board.do: Draw a line AB of 8 cm.

board.say: How long must each half be?

board.do: Ask the child to fold a paper strip end to end and look at the fold.
Write: the fold meets the line at 90 degrees.

misconceptions.repair: Bisect means cut into two equal parts.

misconceptions.ask: Is that one part or the whole line?
What angle does the fold make with the line?
misconceptions.repair: The perpendicular bisector meets at 90 degrees.

misconceptions.ask: Do arcs of 3 cm from each end of 8 cm reach each other?
misconceptions.repair: Use more than half the line, the same for both ends.

checks.question: A 12 cm line is bisected. How long is each part?
At what angle does the perpendicular bisector meet the line?

skills.key_step: The child says perpendicular lines meet at a right angle, at a cross, a T or a corner, and checks with a set square.

floor.question: Is the corner of an exercise book a right angle?

representations: the corner of a door or a window
a set square placed in a corner
lines drawn as a cross, a T and an L
steps: Find where the two lines meet.
Put the corner of a set square there.
If both lines run along its edges, they are perpendicular.
To draw, use the set square or the compass method.
contexts: a flag pole and the ground
the lines of a cross on a road sign

board.do: Draw a cross, a T and an L.

board.say: Do these two lines meet at a right angle?

board.do: Wait for the child to decide.
Ask the child to check each with the corner of a book.

misconceptions.ask: Is a corner a straight line?
Turn the page: are they still at a right angle?
misconceptions.repair: Turning does not change the angle.

misconceptions.ask: Do they meet at a right angle?
misconceptions.repair: Lines that meet at a right angle at a corner are perpendicular.

misconceptions.ask: Does the set square fit exactly?
misconceptions.repair: Perpendicular is exactly 90 degrees: check it.

checks.question: What angle do perpendicular lines make?
Are the two lines of a capital L perpendicular?
